title: Cooperate Fully
warm:
Cooperate fully began in Nolan Greer's penthouse with the soft alibi already warm on [player_name]'s tongue and Detective Imani Brooks's file cooling toward something colder downstairs. Crownspire's glass threw city light across the marble like a jury that had not yet been sworn. Vivienne's unused perfume still breathed from the master bath. Nolan's cufflinks clicked once when he said, "If you stay soft for me through this window, I keep you inside the protection. If you flinch, Pell drafts you out of the story and I stop standing between you and whatever Brooks is becoming."

[player_name] was early thirties, across the hall, cover that had learned the shape of his mouth. She did not ask if Vivienne had left willingly, been paid to vanish, died, or staged the thinning calendar—weekly to monthly to gone—because naming a preferred ending would make her either prophet or accomplice. Brooks's interest was escalating toward homicide without a body on any table. Hope and dread shared the wine ring between them.

"Full cooperation means what, exactly?" she asked.

"Means you open what I open," Nolan said. He glanced toward the locked drawer she had never been permitted to touch—finance-holding silence nested in wood and metal. "Means you walk Brooks through dinners, elevators, empty nights that sound ordinary. Means you do not invent a corpse for a file that wants one. Means you stay across the hall when she knocks and here when she leaves." His mouth tipped—brutal charm, never clean-cut. "It also means you stop pretending the soft alibi is temporary."

Wind sheer pressed the glass. The private elevator chimed faintly in the shaft. Somewhere below, Rhea Quinn was choosing how much slate to surrender; somewhere in a car, Marcus Pell was polishing the word traveling until it reflected nothing. [player_name] tasted oak and the shape of a calendar she had almost confessed.

She could open the locked drawer with him watching—full coop, full risk, silent-partner teeth possibly rhyming with Vivienne's absence without confirming fate. Or she could keep one unnamed night sealed even while wearing cover: the night the black car idled too long, the bag by the door, the perfume bottle opened and capped as if someone changed their mind mid-exit. Withholding was its own cooperation and its own betrayal.

Nolan moved close enough that cologne and rain-money found her. "Brooks is not only missing-persons anymore. You can hear it in how she asks about last sightings. She is hunting for a colder story. Soft is still what keeps you from becoming the sharpest edge in it."

[player_name] walked once past the bath corridor, past perfume that should not still be there, back to the wine ring and the man who made absence sound like care. "If I open the drawer, I become your co-author. If I keep one night unnamed, I become a co-author with a private footnote."

"Both keep you under my protection tonight," he said. "Neither settles Vivienne. I need you to understand that. Four doors stay open. I am not asking you to close one. I am asking you to stand in the hallway with me while Brooks tries."

She set her glass inside his ring until the circles nested. Cooperate fully had a body temperature. Protection had a cost that tasted like wine and unfinished honesty. Across the hall, her own apartment waited with clearer—though not clean—conscience. Here, the soft alibi asked her to choose which kind of full she could survive: the kind that unlocked wood with him watching, or the kind that left one night unnamed even as cover sealed around her mouth.

Elevator chime. Cufflink tick. Perfume. Badge somewhere below rewriting hush into timeline. Vivienne nowhere and everywhere. [player_name] felt the choice hurt before she made it, which was how she knew both verbs were real.

She catalogued the penthouse the way Brooks would: wine ring, locked drawer, bath corridor, private elevator's soft chime, cufflinks that lied audibly. Soft cooperation was not a single yes. It was a sequence of yeses that could still branch. Nolan watched her catalogue him and did not interrupt. Men who purchased silence learned when to let the buyer invent her own receipt.

"Protection is not love," [player_name] said. "Protection is a product. I am trying to decide if I am purchasing it or being packaged inside it."

"Both," Nolan answered, almost kind. "Crownspire sells both in the same box. The difference is whether you open the drawer with your eyes open—or keep one night as the only inventory that still belongs only to you."
